title: Sternal angle (manubriosternal joint) at three lung volumes

quantity.name: sternal angle
quantity.definition: angle between the y-axes of the manubrium and sternal-body coordinate systems (angle of Louis), and its change between poses

source.authors: Beyer B, Feipel V, Sholukha V, Cheze L, Van Sint Jan S
source.sample: 12 asymptomatic volunteers (7 M, 5 F); 12 asymptomatic adults, retrospective spiral CT at TLC, MIC, FRC (same sample as Beyer 2014/2015 CVJ studies per the authors)

protocol.summary: CT-based manubrium and sternum frames at TLC, MIC, FRC.
how_to_use: If the manubrium and sternal body are separate bodies, allow ~4.4 deg of manubriosternal flexion between TLC and FRC (sternal angle larger at higher lung volume), roughly half above and half below MIC.
Otherwise use as a check that a rigid sternum assumption ignores a few degrees of motion.

measurement.device: Siemens SOMATOM spiral CT, 0.5 mm slices, 1 mm spacing; virtual palpation of 5 landmarks per bone (lhpFusionBox)
measurement.posture: supine, breath-hold against closed airway (spirometer-controlled), upper limbs raised above head
measurement.task: static breath-holds at TLC, MIC and FRC

protocol.notes: The paper says all results are mean +- SE, but Fig 3 error bars (~1.6 deg) equal 5.5/sqrt(12); the +- values in the text (5.5, 5.2, 4.9) are therefore SDs and are stored as sd. Differences TLC-MIC p=0.016 and MIC-FRC/TLC-FRC p=0.0011.

extraction.check_notes: Values re-read from text; Fig 3 means 16.7/14.9/12.4 consistent.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
